*This is a sample reflection to show how the quarterly history series works. It can be replaced or kept as the first entry.*

The Innovative Design Scientific Working Group was founded on a straightforward premise: that well-designed clinical trials are among the most powerful tools available for bringing safe and effective treatments to patients, and that the statistical community had a responsibility to advance the methods that make those trials possible.

In the group's early years, innovative trial design was often seen as a specialist concern, of interest to a handful of methodologists but disconnected from the day-to-day work of drug development. The founding members set out to change that, building a community where statisticians, clinicians, regulators, and patient advocates could work together on the practical problems of master protocols, adaptive designs, and trials for rare diseases.

What began as a working group under the Drug Information Association has since grown into a cross-industry community of roughly 200 members spanning the United States, Europe, and Japan, now operating under the DahShu umbrella. The sub-teams have multiplied, the publications have accumulated, and the group's work has helped shape regulatory thinking on both sides of the Atlantic.

The chapters that follow, contributed quarterly by members of the community, tell that story in more detail, and in the words of the people who lived it.
